approach: Enforce the boundary at the lowest shared write points, by remote name and by target repository, and keep the change small. (1) athena-git lib.rs gets `ORIGIN` and `require_origin`, called first in `Git::push_branch` and `Git::push_if_remote_at`. Every records-branch push (landing sink, attribution checkpoint, cutover import) ends in one of these two, so they are covered without touching records_branch.rs, records.rs or reconcile.rs. (2) athena-core remote.rs gets `require_origin`, called first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`. It also gets `origin_url`, which reads origin's fetch and push URLs, compares them by owner/name when both are https github.com URLs and by exact string otherwise, and refuses a split or multi-valued push URL. It gets `origin_client`, which returns a GitHub client only for an https github.com origin. (3) landing.rs builds its client with `origin_client`. early.rs reads origin through `origin_url` and uses `ORIGIN`. This follows the accepted reading (guard in remote.rs, landing.rs and early.rs). Tests use temp git repos with `origin` and `upstream` bare remotes, the existing `ScriptRunner`/`UnreachedHost` and the early-seam `EarlyFake`; no network. The spec entry is filled and pinned by a test. CHANGELOG.md stays untouched, as criterion 7 requires.

decisions.choice: Narrow the file set to the listed deliverables plus one extra file, crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs. Drop gh/mod.rs, gh/records.rs, reconcile.rs and athena-git records_branch.rs. (Answers findings 1-5.)
decisions.reason: `origin_client` and `origin_url` are private-module items in gh/remote.rs. landing.rs, early.rs and gh/tests.rs are descendants of `gh`, so they reach them as `super::remote::...` (remote.rs is declared `mod remote;` at mod.rs:40). That needs no re-export, so mod.rs is not touched. reconcile.rs is not a publishing path: its only host question is `merged_pr(commit)` (reconcile.rs:74, 284) and it writes only to origin through the records sink, so it stays untouched and the lookalike-path point is named as a read-only limit. `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` (records.rs:86) and `append_to_remote_with_hook` (records_branch.rs:413) both end in `push_branch` / `push_if_remote_at` (records_branch.rs:442-444), so one guard in lib.rs covers them; their tests live in gh/tests.rs. lib.rs is kept because it is the single choke point for the three production records pushes (records.rs:156, 365; attribution.rs:785; records_import.rs:206), and the request's Files line allows crates/. This is the root-cause default: guard where the push is made.

rejected.option: Guard only GitRemote and leave the athena-git helpers
rejected.why: Leaves three production git push paths with a free remote name.

rejected.option: Add guards in records_branch.rs, records.rs and reconcile.rs as well
rejected.why: Widens the file set. The lib.rs guard already refuses those pushes. The only unguarded step is the read `sync_from`, which cannot write to the remote.
The records branch push would still accept any remote name.

decisions.choice: Allow exactly the remote name `origin` (case-sensitive) through `athena_git::require_origin`. The empty string, `origin2`, `Origin` and `upstream` are refused with a message that names OLY-B-BND-01.
decisions.reason: Every production caller passes the literal origin: landing.rs:865, early.rs:376 and 460, attribution DEFAULT_REMOTE, main.rs:1751. The existing athena-git tests (lib.rs:1385-1457, records_branch.rs:846-1048), gh/tests.rs and the athena-gate tests push to "origin", so none break. The existing empty-argument refusal at lib.rs:1415 still errors, because `require_origin` runs first and also errors.

rejected.option: Compare the remote URL with the project's GitHub repository
rejected.why: A clone's origin may point anywhere; the PR target is parsed from origin itself.

decisions.choice: `origin_client(git, runner, log, ui) -> Result<GhClient>` in remote.rs is the single place landing builds its GitHub client. It calls `origin_url` and then `GhClient::origin_repository` (client.rs:1026), the strict https + host rule early.rs already uses, and fails when the result is `None`.
decisions.reason: `parse_remote` finds the host by substring (client.rs:1199), so a local path such as `<dir>/github.com/owner/project` became a PR target. One function builds the client, so a test of it is not circular with the land_pr call site. A missing origin or an unsupported one errors in `land_pr` before the GitRemote, the records sink and `attempt()` exist (landing.rs:865-893 then 896+); all pushes, records writes and PR calls happen only inside `attempt()`.

rejected.why: The substring rule lets a lookalike local path name an upstream owner/repo as the PR target.
It is tested directly (gh/tests.rs:1187-1197) and used by `origin_repository`; changing it widens the job.

decisions.choice: `origin_url(git)` reads `git remote get-url origin` and `git remote get-url --push origin`. It refuses when the push output has more than one line. When both URLs are https github.com URLs it compares `GhClient::origin_repository(fetch)` with `GhClient::origin_repository(push)`; otherwise it requires exact string equality (after trim). (Answers finding 8.)
decisions.reason: `git push origin` honors `remote.origin.pushurl` and `pushInsteadOf`, while the PR target comes from the fetch URL. A split would send the push to one repository and the PR to another. Comparing owner/name accepts harmless spellings of the same repository: `parse_remote` strips a trailing `/` and `.git` (client.rs:1197-1198) and `origin_repository` drops userinfo (client.rs:1032-1034). A fetch/push pair where one is GitHub and the other is not falls to string equality and is refused. The error text names OLY-B-BND-01 and does not echo either URL.

rejected.option: Raw string comparison of the two URLs
rejected.why: Refuses a `.git` / no-`.git` pair or a push URL with userinfo, and landing then fails outright.

rejected.option: Only name the split-URL gap in the spec
rejected.why: The check is two git calls and is testable.

decisions.choice: Test the early path's new rule with its own test, `the_early_step_skips_when_origins_push_url_differs_from_its_fetch_url` in gh/tests.rs. It uses `crate::code_health::tests::set_up()` (gh/tests.rs:4898 already does) and `early_seam::install` with an `EarlyFake`. (Answers finding 6.)
decisions.reason: `github_repository` (early.rs:363) is checked before `push_ci_branch` (:388), `delete_ci_branch` (:406) and `early_pr` (:429). Origin is set to `https://github.com/example/project.git` and `remote.origin.pushurl` to a local path. The three entry points are then called and the fake must record no calls. A control with a push URL that differs only by `.git` must record exactly one `push`, which shows the fake can observe the calls and that the accepted spelling still passes. If `github_repository` kept its old `get-url origin` call, the split case would record a push and the test would fail.

rejected.why: Its `early_run` helper (run_pin_tests.rs:413) only adds a fetch URL and lives in a file outside the deliverables.

decisions.choice: Land-level ordering is shown by reading and by the unit tests, not by a new end-to-end land test. (Answers finding 9.)
decisions.reason: Building a verified job record for `Athena::land_pr` needs the cli drain fixtures. The core rig `land_pr_records_worktree_decides_which_job_is_found` (gh/tests.rs:4894) has no verification record, so `land_pr` stops before the origin lookup. The plan therefore (a) puts the `origin_client(...)?` call before `config_at`, `GitContent`, `GitRemote`, `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` and `attempt` (landing.rs:868-933), with every write inside `attempt`; (b) tests the same refusal against a repository with only an `upstream` remote and no origin: `origin_client` is Err with zero runner calls, and `GitRemote{name:"origin"}.push` is Err with upstream refs unchanged; (c) leaves the existing cli land tests (drain.rs:3114, 3142, https origin) as the proof that the happy path still works. The demonstration says so.

rejected.option: Add a land-level test with a hand-built verified job
rejected.why: Needs records and candidate fixtures that exist only in athena-cli; this would widen the job.

decisions.reason: Accepted criterion 7 says CHANGELOG.md, athena.toml and defaults.toml are untouched, and the request's Files line is `docs/spec.toml, crates/`.

decisions.reason: The xtask presence check does not pin the named files or the test name. A measure that does not end `status: not shown` or a known label is a gap (hestia.rs:1229-1238).

steps: In crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs add `pub const ORIGIN: &str = "origin"` and `pub fn require_origin(remote: &str) -> Result<()>`. It returns `GitError::Refused("refused: push to remote {remote:?}; Athena publishes only to origin (OLY-B-BND-01)")` unless `remote == ORIGIN`. Call it as the first statement of `Git::push_branch` (:432) and `Git::push_if_remote_at` (:384, before the empty-argument check). Add tests named `non_origin_*` in the test module near lib.rs:1370: a work repo with bare `origin` and `upstream`; seed upstream by a direct push; both helpers with `upstream`, `""`, `origin2` and `Origin` return Err and the upstream listing is unchanged; both helpers with `origin` succeed.

In crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs add `pub fn require_origin(name: &str) -> Result<()>` (maps `athena_git::require_origin`) and call it as the first statement of `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`, before any `self.git.run`. Add `pub(super) fn origin_url(git: &Git) -> Result<String>`: run `remote get-url origin` and `remote get-url --push origin`, trim both, bail if the push output has more than one line, and accept when both are https github.com URLs with equal `GhClient::origin_repository`, or when the strings are equal. The bail text names OLY-B-BND-01 and does not echo the URLs. Add `pub(super) fn origin_client<'a>(git: &Git, runner: &'a dyn Runner, log: Option<&'a HostErrorLog>, ui: Option<&'a dyn Ui>) -> Result<GhClient<'a>>`: `origin_url`, then `GhClient::origin_repository`, else bail `origin is not an https github.com repository`; build with `GhClient::new` and set `log` and `ui`. Do not change the `Remote` trait. Keep the `concat!` pinned-force flag.

In landing.rs `Athena::land_pr` replace lines 865-867 and the client construction at 881-886: use `athena_git::ORIGIN` for `remote_name`; call `origin_client(&self.git, runner, Some(&log), Some(ui))?` right after the candidate read and before `config_at`, `GitContent`, `GitRemote`, `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` and `attempt`; take `repository` from `client.repository` and the host name from the `HOST` constant early.rs uses. In early.rs use `athena_git::ORIGIN` in `with_ci_remote` and `early_pr_to`, and make `github_repository` use `super::remote::origin_url(&self.git).ok()` and then `https_github_repository`.
Do not touch records.rs, records_branch.rs, reconcile.rs or gh/mod.rs. Their pushes are covered by step 1, and reconcile is read-only toward the host.

Edit docs/spec.toml OLY-B-BND-01. mechanism = "`require_origin` in crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs refuses GitRemote push, replace and delete_branch to any remote but origin; `origin_client` and `origin_url` there give landing a GitHub client only for an https github.com origin whose push and fetch URLs name the same repository, and the early pull request and CI branch steps use the same origin check; `require_origin` in crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs guards push_branch and push_if_remote_at, which every records-branch push uses. Assumes origin is the project's own repository. Not covered: direct Git::run pushes outside those helpers, reads of a non-origin remote, and reconcile's read-only host question. Agents' push and write-form gh are denied separately by crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs." owner stays Themis. measure = "cargo test -p athena-core git_remote_refuses_push_replace_and_delete_to_a_non_origin_remote and cargo test -p athena-core origin_client show that a non-origin push is refused and the PR target is origin's own repository; status: not shown". Leave CHANGELOG.md, athena.toml and defaults.toml untouched.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, then `cargo test -p athena-core --test external_calls_guard`, `--test refusal_corpus`, `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo test -p xtask --test spec --test policy`. Mutation checks, each restored afterwards and recorded in the report: (a) remove `require_origin` from `GitRemote::push`, confirm the criterion 3 test fails; (b) revert `github_repository` to `get-url origin`, confirm the early split test fails; (c) drop the push-URL comparison from `origin_url`, confirm the `origin_client` split case fails.

risks.risk: Landing now accepts only an https github.com origin (the early path already did). An SSH-style or plain-http origin that `parse_remote` accepted (gh/tests.rs:1187-1192) is refused for landing, and a split push URL is refused for landing and the early path.
risks.mitigation: Matches the system fact that SSH remotes are refused at admission and the early path's rule (early.rs:329). The error says why. Existing land tests use the https GITHUB constant (drain.rs:3114). Raised as a Host question.

risks.risk: The guard assumes origin is the project's own repository. A plain clone of a third-party project has origin pointing at that project, and nothing here detects it. The guard also does not stop code that runs `git push` through `Git::run` directly, and the records writer's `sync_from` still reads a non-origin remote before the push is refused.
risks.mitigation: The spec mechanism states these limits so Themis can see what is not covered. The accepted reading makes the same assumption. Reads cannot change the remote; the only local effect is on the local records ref.

risks.risk: reconcile.rs still builds its client with the substring `parse_remote`, so a lookalike local origin can still name a host repository for reconcile's read-only `merged_pr` question.
risks.mitigation: Out of the write boundary: reconcile issues no outbound write. It is named in the spec mechanism. Changing it would need reconcile.rs and the cli reconcile test, outside the deliverables.

risks.risk: Direct `GitRemote` calls check the name only; the split push URL is refused in landing (`origin_client`) and the early path (`github_repository`), not inside `GitRemote::push`.
risks.mitigation: Every production `GitRemote` is built after `origin_url` has run: landing via `origin_client`, early via `github_repository`. The spec text names this limit.

risks.risk: A pre-existing test pushes through a non-origin name that Grep missed.
risks.mitigation: Grep over `push_branch(`, `push_if_remote_at(`, `append_to_remote(` and `GitRemote{` found only "origin" or a variable set to origin. The producer runs the full `cargo test --locked` and the other crates' suites in criterion 6.

risks.risk: Lifetime friction when `land_pr` takes `log` and `ui` through `origin_client`.
risks.mitigation: `GhClient` fields are references and plain values (client.rs:478-488), so `'a` shrinks freely. `log` is created before the client at landing.rs:881.

risks.risk: No end-to-end test of `Athena::land_pr` with no origin: the ordering rests on statement order in landing.rs.
risks.mitigation: The ordering is checked by reading landing.rs and stated in demonstration 4; the same refusal is tested at `origin_client` and `GitRemote` level. The producer must not move any write before the `origin_client(...)?` call.

demonstrations.method: Real git in temp dirs. Work repo with commits c1 and c2, a bare `origin` and a bare `upstream` (`Git::isolated` as at gh/tests.rs:2681-2699). Seed `upstream` with branch `b` at c1 by a direct `git push upstream`, which shows the push is possible for this user; record upstream's `for-each-ref`. Call `GitRemote{name:"upstream"}` `.push(b,c2)`, `.replace(b,c2,c1)` (the pin is correct, so unguarded it would succeed) and `.delete_branch(b)`: each must be Err containing `OLY-B-BND-01` and the upstream listing must be byte-identical. Repeat for names `""`, `origin2` and `Origin`. Then with name `origin`: push succeeds and `remote_head` is c1, replace to c2 succeeds and `remote_head` is c2, delete_branch succeeds and `remote_head` is None. A second test calls `RecordsWriter::new(&git).append_to_remote("upstream", ...)`: Err, upstream refs unchanged; `append_to_remote("origin", ...)` still writes. athena-git tests cover `push_branch` and `push_if_remote_at` with the same names.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --lib gh::tests::git_remote_refuses_push_replace_and_delete_to_a_non_origin_remote && cargo test -p athena-core --lib gh::tests::records_append_refuses_a_remote_other_than_origin && cargo test -p athena-git non_origin
demonstrations.observes: An error for every non-origin name with upstream refs unchanged; success for origin with the head sequence c1, c2, None; the records append to upstream refused and to origin written.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `require_origin` removed from `GitRemote::push`, the push to `upstream` succeeds, `unwrap_err` panics and the upstream listing differs from the recorded one. The same holds for replace and delete_branch, and for the athena-git helpers and the records append.

Fixture: real temp repos via `Git::isolated` and `tempfile`; no double. The seam exists; the tests add an `upstream` remote (plan steps 1, 2 and 6).

demonstrations.method: The three origin cases, plus the split cases. (a) No origin: in a repo with only a bare `upstream` remote, `origin_client` is Err and the runner (`UnreachedHost`, which fails on any call) has no call; `GitRemote{name:"origin"}.push` is Err and upstream refs are unchanged. (b) Local-path origin and the lookalike `<tmp>/github.com/example/project.git`: `origin_client` is Err and no gh call. A `remote.origin.pushurl` set to a different repository, and a push URL set twice (`git config --add`), are Err with no gh call. (c) Origin `https://github.com/example/project.git`: `origin_client` returns a client for `example/project`, and with `ScriptRunner` `close_pr(9, ..)` makes calls whose paths all start with `repos/example/project/`. A push URL that differs only by `.git`, a trailing slash or userinfo is accepted. A `GitRemote{name:"origin"}` push with `upstream` present changes only origin's bare repository. (d) Early path: origin `https://github.com/example/project.git` with a split `pushurl`: `push_ci_branch`, `early_pr` and `delete_ci_branch` through the early seam record no calls; the control with a `.git`-only difference records one `push`. Landing order: `Athena::land_pr` is not run end to end (the verified-job fixtures exist only in athena-cli). Reading landing.rs shows `origin_client(...)?` before `config_at`, the `GitRemote`, `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` and `attempt()`, and every write happens inside `attempt()`; the cli land tests cover the happy path.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --lib origin_client && cargo test -p athena-core --lib the_early_step_skips_when_origins_push_url_differs_from_its_fetch_url && cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_missing_or_non_github_origin_skips_the_early_step_silently && cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain
demonstrations.observes: Err and zero runner calls with no origin, a local path, a lookalike path, a split push URL and a multi-valued push URL. For the https origin every recorded gh path is under repos/example/project/ and the `.git`/slash/userinfo variants are accepted. The early fake records nothing for the split push URL and one push for the control. The existing early-skip test and the cli land tests still pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `origin_client` used the substring `parse_remote`, the lookalike case would build a client and fail. If `origin_url` ignored `pushurl`, the split cases would fail. If `github_repository` kept its old `get-url origin` call, the early test would see a push. If the client were built for another repository, the path-confinement assertion would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `origin_client` and `origin_url` (added by plan step 2; `origin_client` is called from `Athena::land_pr` by step 3), `Athena::push_ci_branch`, `early_pr` and `delete_ci_branch` (early.rs:384, 405, 425; they exist), `GhClient::close_pr` (exists) and `GitRemote::push`. Fixtures: `Git::isolated` temp repos with `git remote add origin <url>` (an https origin is only a URL string; nothing is fetched or pushed to it), the existing `ScriptRunner` (gh/tests.rs:4794) and `UnreachedHost` (gh/tests.rs:4886), and `EarlyFake` installed with `early_seam::install` (mod.rs:99). `Athena` comes from `crate::code_health::tests::set_up()`. demonstrations.method: Diff review plus a mutation run by the producer. The diff must show the new test asserting `is_err()` plus the `OLY-B-BND-01` text for push, replace and delete_branch to `upstream`, and comparing upstream's ref listing before and after. The producer temporarily removes the `require_origin` call from `GitRemote::push`, runs the criterion 3 test and records the failure at the push-to-upstream assertion in its report, then restores the call. It repeats with the `origin_url` call in `github_repository` (early test fails) and the pushurl comparison in `origin_url` (origin_client test fails). The verifier has no edit command, so it checks the diff and the recorded runs.
demonstrations.observes: Assertions on refusal and on unchanged upstream refs, not wiring only; the recorded mutation run fails at the push-to-upstream assertion.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs, then the other suites that reach the changed paths.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked && cargo test -p athena-core --test external_calls_guard --test refusal_corpus && cargo test -p xtask --test policy --test spec
demonstrations.observes: All pass. This includes the athena-git, athena-gate (attribution checkpoint), athena-core (landing, early, reconcile, cutover import) and athena-cli (land and reconcile) suites. `external_calls_guard` sees no new `gh` or HTTP client name. `refusal_corpus` holds reading checks; this change adds no reading check, parser or stem list, so I cite no case id and no result. The input forms of the new remote-name rule (`origin`, `upstream`, empty, `origin2`, `Origin`) and of the push-URL rule (equal, `.git` spelling, userinfo, split, multi-valued, local path, lookalike path, non-GitHub host) are covered by the unit tests named above, not by corpus cases. The policy test passes because the new text uses neutral words, no email-like text, and the pinned-force flag stays split with `concat!` (remote.rs:61).
